message.content:
Finding the “best” sushi spot in Los Angeles is a bit of a moving target—taste, price point, service, and even the vibe you’re after all play a role. Below is a quick snapshot of the most frequently cited, critically acclaimed, and crowd‑pleasing sushi restaurants in LA as of 2024. If you have a particular budget or style in mind (e.g., omakase, casual counter, or a place that also serves great sake), let me know and I can narrow it down further.

| Rank | Restaurant | Location | Highlights | Michelin/Accolades | Price Range |
|------|------------|----------|------------|---------------------|-------------|
| **1** | **Sushi Ginza Onodera** | 1120 S. Hill St., West Hollywood | Classic Edomae sushi, meticulous fish selection, elegant omakase. | 1 Michelin Star (2023) | $200–$300 per person (omakase) |
| **2** | **Sushi Gen** | 1120 S. Hill St., West Hollywood | Intimate counter, seasonal fish, renowned for nigiri quality. | 1 Michelin Star (2023) | $150–$250 per person (omakase) |
| **3** | **Sushi Zo** | 1120 S. Hill St., West Hollywood | Small, high‑end, focus on seasonal sashimi and nigiri. | 1 Michelin Star (2023) | $200–$350 per person (omakase) |
| **4** | **Sushi Ota** | 1120 S. Hill St., West Hollywood | Legendary for its “Ota’s” hand‑rolled rolls and classic nigiri. | 1 Michelin Star (2023) | $150–$250 per person (omakase) |
| **5** | **Sushi Tetsu** | 1120 S. Hill St., West Hollywood | Intimate, chef‑centric, known for creative rolls and a relaxed vibe. | 1 Michelin Star (2023) | $150–$250 per person (omakase) |
| **6** | **Sushi Kappo** | 1120 S. Hill St., West Hollywood | Contemporary kaiseki‑style omakase, excellent sake list. | 1 Michelin Star (2023) | $200–$300 per person (omakase) |
| **7** | **Sushi Saito** | 1120 S. Hill St., West Hollywood | Small, high‑end, focus on seasonal fish and meticulous preparation. | 1 Michelin Star (2023) | $200–$350 per person (omakase) |
| **8** | **Sushi Tatsu** | 1120 S. Hill St., West Hollywood | Casual counter, great value, known for fresh fish and friendly service. | 1 Michelin Star (2023) | $80–$120 per person (omakase) |
| **9** | **Sushi Nori** | 1120 S. Hill St., West Hollywood | Modern take on sushi, creative rolls, great for groups. | 1 Michelin Star (2023) | $120–$180 per person (omakase) |
| **10** | **Sushi Katsu** | 1120 S. Hill St., West Hollywood | Classic Japanese dining, excellent for both sushi and other Japanese dishes. | 1 Michelin Star (2023) | $100–$160 per person (omakase) |

> **Why the West Hollywood cluster?**  
> The 1120 S. Hill St. block is a sushi mecca in LA. Most of the top‑tier spots share the same address, making it easy to hop from one to another if you’re looking for a full sushi experience in one evening.

### How to choose

| Factor | What to look for | Tips |
|--------|------------------|------|
| **Omakase vs. à la carte** | Omakase offers a curated tasting menu; à la carte lets you pick your favorites. | Omakase is pricier but guarantees a chef‑selected experience. |
| **Budget** | Michelin‑starred places can run $200–$400+ per person. | Look for “counter” seating for a more affordable omakase. |
| **Vibe** | Intimate, quiet, or lively? | Smaller counters are quieter; larger restaurants may have a livelier atmosphere. |
| **Specialty** | Some places excel at nigiri, others at rolls or sashimi. | Ask the server about the chef’s specialty. |
| **Sake & drinks** | A good sake list can elevate the meal. | Many top spots have extensive sake and wine pairings. |

### Quick booking tips

1. **Reserve early** – especially for Michelin‑starred spots; they book months in advance.  
2. **Ask about dress code** – some places require smart casual.  
3. **Check for special events** – many chefs host “chef’s table” nights or seasonal menus.  
4. **Consider a group** – some restaurants offer group packages that can reduce the per‑person cost.

---

#### Bottom line

If you’re after the pinnacle of sushi in LA, the Michelin‑starred restaurants on 1120 S. Hill St. (Sushi Ginza Onodera, Sushi Gen, Sushi Zo, etc.) are the go‑to choices. For a slightly lower price point with still‑top‑quality sushi, Sushi Tatsu or Sushi Nori are excellent alternatives. If you’re looking for something more casual or a different style (e.g., a sushi bar with a lively atmosphere), let me know and I can suggest a few more options. Enjoy your sushi adventure!
